# Plugins (details)

Full reference for every plugin. Read this on demand (e.g. before writing a helper or a test fixture, to check whether one already exists). A plugin's *Test helpers* item lists its `<runtime>/testing/` barrels: shared fixtures that only test code may import. The slim always-loaded index is [`plugins-compact.md`](./plugins-compact.md).

A list longer than 20 values (importers, uses, contributions) is summarized here and in the plugin's CLAUDE.md as one count per group; the linked `REFERENCE.md` beside the plugin lists it in full.

- **`active-data`** — Meta plugin for inline interactive widgets agents render via XML-like tags in assistant text. Sub-plugins contribute block (tag) and code (claimed code-span) renderers, and declare inline chips through primitives/text-editor/inline-chip; hosts use useActiveDataSegments() + useActiveDataLinkify(). Persistent state for inline interactive widgets — table + resource keyed by (conversationId, messageId, tag, occurrenceIndex).

    - **`go`** — Renders <go>…</go> in an agent's reply — a part of the answer the user can pick as their reply — as one tinted unit, [text | ▶]: ▶ sends it back as <go>…</go> (the agent reads the part of its answer the user picked), clicking the text puts it in the draft as an editable tinted region closed by a ✕. One line is inline wherever it is written; a multi-line block is a card with a ✎ / ▶ rail, its `- [ ]` lines pickable rows, or a table whose rows lead with `[ ]` / `[x]` a pickable table (only the picked items are sent — a row as a `- [x]` line of its first cell — and Reset restores the agent's picks). The user's sent message shows the accepted <go> in full, in the same tint.
      - Web:

          - `ActiveData.Tag` "go" → `GoBlock`
          - `InlineTextWalkerSlot`

    - **`id-chip`** — Id chips, web half: idChip({ presenter, surfaces, component? }) mints a kind's IdKinds.Presenter together with its inline chip — the pattern derived from the kind (never re-typed), a generic title + icon chip unless the family brings its own component. rowReferent folds a live by-id row read into a presenter's referent state. Id chips, server half: idChipServer({ kind, surfaces, resolve }) contributes the kind's IdKinds.Referent, the InlineTokenReferentSource that hands a model the referent's title, and — for a chip that belongs in documents — the Editor.InlineToken that keeps a page block holding it agent-readable.

        - **`sync`** — MessageBodyState: one message's mail.message-body value with its loading and failed-fetch (Retry) states drawn once, for every pane that shows a body. Gmail sync engine (on-demand model): a bounded, metadata-only backfill mirrors a recent window of message envelopes; history.list incremental delta keeps them fresh (with a bounded full-resync fallback on historyId expiry) via a scheduled main-only delta tick (the documented no-polling exception). Message bodies + attachments are hydrated lazily on first open by the mail.hydrate job (asked for by a mail.message-body subscriber, or POST /api/mail/hydrate to retry) and cached; the mail.message-body value reads one message's body state from the mirror. The mail.search paged value answers a Gmail search as ranked thread ids, mirroring the envelopes it sees. Mirrors threads/messages/labels into the mail-core tables.

        - **`recording`** — Sonata recording: the session's recording player — the YouTube video whoever shows a song's recording declares (useShowRecording), owned by the playback session so it outlives what shows it: RecordingVideo is only a viewport the playing iframe is moved into (Element.moveBefore, never reloaded) and out of, to an off-screen parking spot, so collapsing its section or switching the display neither stops nor reloads it. When the open score is timed on that video (Score.meta.recording) it is the session's transport driver while ready — the cursor, the synth and the A–B loop follow the video, its rate is the tempo; otherwise it plays on its own with YouTube's controls under a “Not synced” badge. RecordingSwitch turns the video off (the synth plays alone, same timing) and on. The video's on/off persists in the sonata.recording-video config; its sound, level and the sync offset (no control in the card; Settings → Config) in the sonata.recording config. Owns the SonataRecording.Refused seam for whoever picked a video YouTube refuses to embed. Server registration of the Sonata recording mix config and the video on/off config.

        - **`session`** — Sonata playback session: plays a song's composed content — the tempo-scaled score, the rAF transport over a per-surface cursor store, the A–B loop, the count-in, seek / scrub verbs, the play- and seek-on-load intents, a stack of clocks, and a stack of transport drivers (an external medium — a recording — that owns the position while registered). Mountable by any host (useSession); defines the per-session SonataSession.{Provider,Effect} slots the audio plugins contribute to.
          - Web:
            - Slots:
              - `SonataSession.Provider`
              - `SonataSession.Effect`
            - Slot contributors:
              - `SonataSession.Provider` ← `apps.sonata.audio.engine`

              - `SonataSession.Provider` ← `apps.sonata.recording`

        - **`sources`** — Input source sub-plugins for Sonata (MIDI, chord-grid, …).
          - Plugins:
            - **`chord-grid`** — Chord-grid input source for Sonata. A small mini-language (e.g. `Amaj9 Am9 (E E6)`) authors chord annotations: each cell is a bar, a `( )` group shares a bar, and `.` holds the previous chord. A cell may name a chord by letter (`Am7`) or by degree (`vi7`), the latter resolved against the key a `key:` directive declares. compile() emits chord + key annotations only; the shell's reactive re-voicing step generates the notes under the global voicing config. Persists per-song grid text and contributes the library 'New Chord Grid' affordance, hydration, the cell of the Chords field its extension exposes on every list of songs, the song cover (its first chords as degree-coloured chord boxes), and an in-player editor section. Owns the sonata_songs_ext_chord_grid side-table: per-song chord text. Creates chord-grid–backed songs, persists grid edits (syncing the parent song's derived duration only; the title is library-owned), and exposes the chord text to every list of songs (LiveColumns.Expose) for its Chords field and cover.

                - **`alignment`** — UG sheet alignment in the player: a 'Recording' editor section showing the song's YouTube video (the recording plugin's RecordingVideo viewport with its volume, and its on/off RecordingSwitch in the header; the video itself is declared by a headless effect to the session's recording player, so it keeps playing — synced to the transport when the song plays on its alignment, a weak match included, else on its own — while the section is collapsed), an alignment status box (icon, status line, one control — Cancel, Re-align, Retry, Try another or Find a video — and while working a three-stage bar: find a video, analyse the audio, align the sheet), the video's line (title, match chip, channel, Replace) and an inline picker (a YouTube link, the candidate videos with thumbnail and outcome — click one to switch — and Search again); a headless report of a video the player refuses (SonataRecording.Refused → video-refused), and a headless effect writing the applied alignment record into the Ultimate Guitar raw so the Score plays on the recording's beats. In the library: the Video field's presentation (hidden by default). UG sheet alignment server: owns the sonata_songs_ext_ug_alignment side-table (video, who picked it, the resolver's candidates, status, record) served as a lookup-only live collection and its video id exposed to every list of songs (LiveColumns.Expose), the sonata.ug-alignment.align supervised job (choose a video with findSongVideos and walk the best candidates when none was set; beat features → alignChords → record, its live phase written on the row; a user's Cancel stops it as cancelled), the set-video / find-a-video / video-refused / re-align (also resuming a cancelled or failed walk) / cancel / get endpoints, and a trigger that starts choosing a video for a new UG song and re-aligns one whose sheet changes.

        - **`transcription`** — Sonata transcription in the library: a 'Transcribe…' entry in the + menu (a video/post link, or page images and PDFs) that creates the song and starts the transcribing agent; a transcribed song shows its agent run as an embedded agent thread — the steps, the agent's summary and a reply box — in the player until the score is in (Retry when it failed), then in the player's Transcription section, where a reply asks for a correction and the resubmitted score replaces the song's; and a Transcribing / Failed badge and cover on its card. Owns the sonata_songs_ext_transcription side-table: a transcribed song's run state (status, input, task, latest conversation, error). POST transcribe creates the song (MusicXML source), a Sonata task and a transcribing agent in a `sonata.transcription` scratch workspace (CLAUDE.md = the instructions, ./bin/st = the toolkit); its sonata_submit_transcription MCP tool imports the agent's MusicXML into the song. Exposes its status, latest conversation and error to every list of songs (LiveColumns.Expose); a conversation closed before submitting marks the song failed (retry relaunches).

- **`auth`** — Shared authentication infrastructure (OAuth 2.0, API keys, password sign-in). Exposes the Accounts pane — a DataView of every provider (Auth.Provider) and non-provider setup surface (Auth.Integration), grouped by service, each row opening one account pane to the right (header, account, and the row's setup inline — a provider's setup wizard, OAuth client steps or sign-in form; an integration's own setup) — and the Settings app surfaces the Account entry. Worktree-side auth helpers. Provides getTokenFromCentral() for worktree plugins that need OAuth tokens. Centralized OAuth/API-key/password-sign-in infrastructure for third-party services. Tokens persist via the central secrets store; auth runs on the central runtime so all worktrees share one connected state.

- **`backup`** — Backup orchestrator UI: run backups, view history, and open one run's detail pane — whose sections (what went into the archive, where it was dispatched to, and the Grant access repair for a target that lost its OAuth token) are contributed by the backup arm. Backup orchestrator: assembles archives from registered backup sources, dispatches to registered storage targets. The assembly runs OUT OF PROCESS as a supervised job's `run` body, so a backend restart mid-`tar` no longer kills the backup.

  - Plugins:
    - **`runs-arm`** — The backup arm's presence on the merged run surface: its rows' link into the backup run-detail pane, its four scalar columns (native status, archive size, source and target counts) as real filterable and sortable SQL dimensions, and the three detail sections — the archive's size on one line, the manifest's source reports, and the per-target outcome with its Grant access remediation. The backup arm of the unified run space: binds backup_runs into the runs union — its native status folded into the shared outcome vocabulary (partial included, since backup is the only kind that can half-succeed), a label naming what the run covered, and the source / target counts plus the raw per-target results as its own columns. Reads null for namespace (a backup covers the machine, not a checkout — the table's own namespace column is the in-flight index's scope discriminator, not a fact about the run) and for message (a backup's failure words are per-target).

                - **`token-budget`** — The agent's work allowance as a transcript stat: how many tokens the harness has charged against it up to the reading position, summed across the re-anchor it performs on every new request. Owns both halves of the move — the stat, and the filter that takes the harness's repeated reminder rows out of the transcript flow they were cluttering. Serves the token-budget stat's fold of a conversation's transcript before the page's window.

        - **`pending-turn`** — The single entry point for sending a turn from the browser (useSendConversationTurn, bound to the subtree's transport: mints the turn's ledger id, shows its echo at once, then runs its delivery), and the view of the server's turn ledger (conversations/turn-ledger): usePendingTurns merges a conversation's live ledger rows with this tab's sends whose row has not arrived, PendingTurnCard renders each by state (echo while held or being typed, a warning when the CLI merged it with leftover text, Retry + Copy to draft when it failed), and useOptimisticConversationStatus reads a conversation as working from the instant a turn is sent.     - **`runtime-sdk`** — The health report's Claude Code row: Claude Code itself (critical while missing or signed out, with the install / sign-in commands and Check again), attention when it differs in major.minor from the CLI version the pinned Agent SDK was built for, the agent processes running — here, and in every other worktree (each as its task's chip) — the active Claude account's usage limits as meters (the week collapsed, the session too expanded; attention while its limit is reached), and the Claude account picker (each account's weekly room, add / remove / switch, auto-switch, Continue on another account when the active one is limited). The sdk runtime's portable half: the conversations_ext_sdk_agent side table (each agent's event cursor and the projection of its events — session id, busy/idle, the open question, the last turn and its rewind anchor), the pure event reducer, and the mapping of a launch onto the agent's options file; the runtime-sdk.error-stopped collection (active conversations whose agent's turn an API error stopped — a usage limit, a server error, a lost connection — with the CLI's kind of failure).

    - **`latency-ledger`** — The browser half of the latency ledger: times every page load and in-app navigation until every list on screen has its data, and the delay of every update pushed into the tab, and posts them as per-minute histograms at most once a minute.     - **`sentinel`** — Sentinel web presence: registers the sentinel config (sampler cadence + onset thresholds) for Settings → Config, the one-line duress-episode and sentinel-down report summaries for Debug → Reports, and the health report's Machine watcher row (critical while main's watcher is down or its process is gone or the disk is nearly full, attention while it restarts, the machine is under duress or the disk is low or filling fast, read from the sentinel.status push resource), with its stats — load per core, free memory, free disk and builds at a glance, and, when expanded, each signal that can trip duress against its limit — read from the sentinel.vitals push resource — and where the machine's CPU and memory go (machine-usage). Cluster congestion sentinel: a main-only always-on sampler + onset detector + duress-latch lifecycle on a dedicated worker thread (host load, Postgres-side wait/lock/IO pressure, fleet state, per-backend health rollup, compressor pressure), feeding the 'cluster' trace ring so every trace gains a cluster-vitals lane, congestion onset is observable, and the latch lease survives a wedged main loop. Persists duress episodes as trip/clear lines on the duress-episodes channel (readDuressEpisodes). Reports the watcher's own supervision status: a host-global status file written on every transition, served on every backend as the sentinel.status push resource (with the duress latch), and a sentinel-down report when main gives up respawning it. Its worker writes the latest reading to a host-global vitals file every tick, served on every backend as the sentinel.vitals push resource.

    - **`stuck-spans`** — Stuck-span report renderer: a one-line Debug → Reports summary for the span-stuck kind (how long it has been running, the chain of operations it is stuck under, and a View-trace chip). Stuck-span watchdog: a 15 s interval on each backend's own event loop — deliberately NOT a scheduled job — that reads the runtime profiler's open entries and files a span-stuck report while an http / sub / loader / push / flush / cascade span is still running past its threshold (90 s — past the app pool's 60 s query deadline; http 120 s), once per span run, naming the deepest stuck span of a chain with its open ancestors and attaching one coherent-instant trace per tick. Catches the hang a completion-time slow-op report never can. duressExempt; job and bg spans are excluded.

          - `serverEntryFor` — The registry entry of `pluginPath`'s server barrel, as codegen writes one (`<id>` the dotted path, loaded by its `@plugins/<path>/server` specifier), with the `dependsOn` the caller states.
          - `withHostServices` — Run `fn` with `providers` (each a `Svc.provide(impl)`) answering their services — over the unbooted host's providers and over a collected graph's — and put the previous answers back once it settles, so a suite swapping a service cannot leak it into the suites after it in the same bun process.

- **`hints`** — The hints engine, web half: Hints.Hint / Hints.Tour declarations, useHintAnchor (ref registration, holding a floating toolbar open while its tip shows), useHintMoment (a tip shown once at its moment, lowest order first, one at a time), startTour / autoStart, emitHintSignal, the seen state and catalog reads — and the one HintHost at Core.Root drawing the active tip (halo + card) or the tour's welcome card / spotlit step on one persistent stage — every change of scene a CSS transition of the same elements — in the hints' own fixed theme (the same look in every app), every tour end pulsing ? and toasting where the tour lives. Background activity catalog: defineBackgroundKind registers a provider (a mechanism that runs things on its own: jobs, warm-ups, timers) that lists its entries with trigger, scope and latest run, its recent runs and an optional Run now; the catalog merges every provider into the pushed background.catalog value (throttled), serves background.recent-runs per entry and POST /api/background/run-now, fills event-triggered entries' event names from contributed BackgroundTriggerSource annotations, and names no provider.     - **`file-watcher`** — defineFileWatcher: the one declared in-process file watcher — a named, described declaration (static policy: extensions, ignore, debounce, ceiling, writesWhileOpen, depth, reconcile, mainOnly) whose start({dirs, label, onChange, onReconcile}) opens instances over one @parcel/watcher engine (debounce + ceiling flush, reconcile timer, kqueue sizing). Records per declaration its open instances, last change batch and a ring of handler runs for the Background activity catalog (onWatcherActivity / listFileWatchers / fileWatcherRecentRuns). The cli barrel's watchForCommand is the same engine for a foreground command, with no registry. acquireDirWatch({dir, scope, onChange}) is the shared directory-watch hub: one native watch per folder tree, refcounted, a dir under a watched root riding its watch, with subtree or children (depth-1 listing) scope — a children request with no root above it opening only a single-directory watch (depth children, fs.watch), never a recursive one.

    - **`ssh`** — Hermetic SSH client primitive: sshRun (one remote command) and sshUpload (one file, over scp) open a session to (host, port, user) with EXACTLY the private key they are given — IdentitiesOnly + IdentityAgent=none + -F /dev/null keep the machine's own agent, config and multiplexed sessions out, so a connection test proves the key it was handed works — and return a discriminated result whose failures are classified from OpenSSH stderr (dns / unreachable / timeout / auth / host-key-mismatch / command-failed / unknown). Both are built from one shared hermetic invocation, so the isolation flags cannot drift between them. Host-key policy is pinned-or-learn with no 'off'; the key is materialized 0600 into a mkdtemp dir removed in finally. An upload lands on a staging sibling and is renamed over its destination, so it can neither fail because the destination is being executed nor leave a truncated file where a working one was.

    - **`youtube`** — Embedded YouTube player the app controls: loadYouTubeIframeApi (the IFrame API, loaded once), <YouTubePlayer controller videoId loop autoplay audio onReady onPlaying onError onStateChange/> bound to a useYouTubePlayer() controller (without controls the iframe takes no pointer and its thumbnail covers it until it first plays, so none of YouTube's chrome shows, and a click opens the video on youtube.com at the playhead) (play, pause, isPlaying, isAdvancing, playRange for one pass then back to the loop, seek — re-cueing a video that has not started rather than starting it — getCurrentTime, getDuration, getPlaybackRate, setPlaybackRate resolving to the rate the video took), useYouTubePlayerState, useYouTubePlayhead (one read per animation frame while playing), and createMediaClock (a smoothed, slewed reading of the playhead for something slaved to it). Loops without polling: one timer to the loop's end, reset on every state change. Server-side YouTube: checkOembed(videoId) asks oEmbed whether a video plays in an embed (status code mapped by the core's statusFromOembedCode, plus the title and channel of a 200), and searchYouTube(query, exec) lists YouTube's results for a query (id, title, channel, duration, views, verified, art track) through yt-dlp's flat search, from the on-demand `youtube-audio` dependency this plugin owns.

A video YouTube will not serve throws YouTubeAudioUnavailableError (non-retryable); a stream YouTube refuses (HTTP 403, intermittent) is re-extracted with a freshly signed URL and retried up to 3 times; still refused, or another download error of the video, throws YouTubeAudioDownloadError — isYouTubeAudioError answers 'the video's failure, not the machine's' for both. A bot check, rate limit or unreachable YouTube throws YouTubeAccessError (retryable, the machine's failure). Failures come back from the Python module as a classified document, never a traceback. The daily youtube-audio.sweep keeps the cache within 30 days unused and 2 GB.

              - `YouTubeAccessError` — This machine cannot get audio from YouTube right now, whatever the video: a bot check or rate limit on its IP (`blocked`), or YouTube cannot be reached (`network`).
              - `YouTubeAudioDownloadError` — This video's download failed in a way that may clear later: YouTube still refused its audio stream (HTTP 403) after re-extracting it, or another download error on this video (a broken format).
              - `YouTubeAudioUnavailableError` — YouTube will not serve this video to anyone: unavailable, private, removed, age-gated.

- **`network`** — Umbrella for how data moves between the server and the browser: the live-resource API (declare a collection, query it, serve it) and, later, the live-state primitives it is built on.
  - Plugins:
    - **`live`** — Unified live-resource API, read half: useLive (a collection's window — where/orderBy/limit with canGrow/growing/loadMore — a grouping of a filterable column's values with counts, grown by its limit, a collection declared `all` whole — every row in its declared order, or a select-scoped slice of it — or an explicit id set), useLiveRow (one row: loading, failed, found, or determinately absent), with mapRow reducing a row read to a ResourceResult of what the row means; useLive also reads a typed-query liveValue (its question encoded to one canonical tuple); every collection's window — and a key-range-paged liveValue — is read as key-range pages — bounded windows tiling the order by server-minted row-key cuts, split when full and merged when small — given a measured viewport (useLive(c, q, { viewport })) with no depth limit, the pages near it live and the rest held stale up to a per-reader budget, past which they are height-keeping placeholders drawn before and after the rows, and without one every page live, capped at maxLimit rows; FieldPresentation.Register presents an owner's fields — an entity's own, an extension's exposed ones, a union arm's, a collection's own — with their cells, widths and live options in every list that reaches the owner, read by useFieldPresentations. Unified live-resource API, server half: serveValue (a liveValue's loader, from Postgres — change-feed driven, a collection-shaped payload must declare `unbounded: { reason }` — or from an external source with notify(); pushed by default, or refetched over HTTP when the liveValue declares `load: "on-demand"`; a typed-query value's hooks and notify take the decoded question, and a key-range-paged one — external only — is loaded one key range at a time, each answer checked against its range and minted its `$key`, notify(q) reaching every subscribed page and the per-question meta sibling, and sliceRange answers a range for a list held in memory) and serveCollection (binds a liveCollection's row fields to a table's columns — the projection is exactly the row schema — ANDs an optional base `where` into every read, and compiles its window + `:rows` point resources through windowQueryResource and its `:groups` GROUP BY push value — only `:rows` for a lookup-only collection, and the whole ordered set (`key`, a routed scopedMembership alias compiled by compileAllCollection) + `:rows` for one declared `all` — encoding a column type's declared wire form in JS per row; a collection reaching an entity compiles at boot, folding every LiveColumns.Expose contribution of an extension exposing fields of it — and a `columnScope` collection every LiveColumns.Scoped set — into its rows' `$columns`) — or, `source: "external"`, from a source outside Postgres that answers window / rows / groups / count / all by hand (core's serveCollectionOn: every answer checked against the row schema, every window row's `$key` minted, notify() re-reading the subscribed tuples); every filter compiles through the filter language's filterSql. Unified live-resource API, central half: serveValue for a liveValue declared `origin: "central"` — the external arm only (central has no change feed), registered through the central plugin's `resources: [served]`; its options compile through the same code as the worktree serveValue.

- **`packages`** — Umbrella for package management utilities.
  - Plugins:
    - **`canonical-params`** — One spelling per live-resource params tuple: canonicalParams drops an undefined param and a "" for a declared-optional one, and canonicalJson spells a structured param (a typed-query value's q) one way — keys sorted at every depth, non-JSON refused. The single rule both ends of the live-state wire apply (the browser's useResource and the resource runtime), so they cannot drift.
      - Cross-plugin:
        - Imported by:
          - `apps/deploy/analytics/dashboard`
          - `framework/resource-runtime`
          - `network/live`
      - Core:
        - Exports (values):
          - `canonicalJson`
          - `canonicalParams`
    - **`coalesce`** — Trigger coalescer: createCoalescer / createKeyedCoalescer run a reaction at most once at a time per key and fold every trigger that lands mid-run into ONE trailing run (its items merged), so however many triggers arrive the work is bounded to one running plus one pending per key — and a trigger never joins a run that started before it.
      - Core:
        - Exports (types):
          - `Coalescer`
          - `CoalescerStats`
          - `KeyedCoalescer`
        - Exports (values):
          - `createCoalescer`
          - `createKeyedCoalescer`
    - **`flock`** — Kernel advisory file locking: flockTry/flockRelease over libc flock(2), and waitForFlock — a push-based blocking acquire run in a child so the event loop never freezes. The one lock ownership the kernel releases on process death (SIGKILL included) and that consults no pid.
      - Cross-plugin:

          - `framework/tooling/checks`

      - Test helpers:
        - Web: `@plugins/primitives/plugins/data-view/web/testing`
          - `consumerPaging` — A consumer's paging (`DataViewProps.paging`): placeholders before and after the rows, every viewport report pushed to `reports`, nothing to grow.
          - `deriveFields` — {@link useDerivedFields}, pure.
          - `describePagedConformance` — The paged-view contract every DataView view honours, run against `view` mounted through the real body on a laid-out page (`mountPagedDataView`):
          - `lowerFilterGroup` — Lower a DataView `FilterGroup` into a filter-language `Filter`, each rule through its operator's `lower` with `ctx.column` = the field id.
          - `lowersToMatch` — Does a rule `op(operand)` keep a row whose field projects to `value`? — the in-memory evaluator's exact path for one rule: `op.lower` over a column of `domain` (an incomplete rule, `undefined`, keeps every row), the DataView domain adapter, then the filter language's `matchesFilter`.
          - `mountPagedDataView` — Mount ONE view of a paged DataView against a laid-out page — through the real seam (`DataViewShellFrame` around `DataViewBody`, the body every DataView renders), with a fake one-instance view model, inside a scroller whose `scrollTop` the test drives and an IntersectionObserver that answers from the layout, as a browser does.
          - `PAGED_VIEWPORT_PX` — The scroller's visible height.
          - `renameColumns` — Rename every clause's column through `rename` (field id → column name).
          - `resolveLiveFields` — Resolve a schema against a live source — and check it where it is declared.
          - `testField` — A minimal option-less field for a test that calls `op.lower` directly.
          - Types: `PagedDataView`, `PagedLayout`, `PagedViewUnderTest`

Restores the characters a rendering replaced (an active-data chip's `token`), and removes the newlines a chip's blockified label box injects mid-sentence. Yields to any handler that already prevented the default, and never acts inside a contenteditable. A substituting element also SELECTS as one unit: its letters take no highlight, and a selectionchange listener rings the whole element while the selection overlaps it — so the selection shows exactly what the copy will carry.

        - **`web-storage`** — The one door to browser storage (localStorage / sessionStorage): defineStore declares an owner — key prefix s:<owner>:, byte cap, TTL, what to do when full (evict-oldest for caches, refuse for what the user typed), a zod schema — and returns a typed read/write/remove/subscribe handle with one {v, ts} envelope. The caps of an area's owners sum under the browser's quota (asserted at declaration and statically by the budget-fits check), so no owner can fill storage for another. Every refused write and unreadable entry is announced (onStorageFailure); useStorageUsage and scanArea feed the health row; the no-raw-web-storage lint rule bans touching Web Storage anywhere else.

    - **`metrics`** — Metrics surfaces: useMetricCatalog / useMetric / useMetricDetails / useMetricDetailsTotal (live reads of the served metrics values — the details one key-range pages, every loaded one live, and its total the per-question meta sibling — so a change the metric's source announces refetches what is on screen, without polling), MetricTile (KPI toggle with value, polarity-coloured delta and sparkline), MetricCard (controls derived from the catalog entry: split, daily | cumulative for flows, table twin, previous-period line on the unsplit total), BreakdownCard, RangeBar, the DrillDrawer listing the records behind a bucket, BoardView (sections of focus tiles, a lead card and a card grid, every ref checked against the catalog) and Board (a view-core tabbed board whose specs live in a config declared with defineBoardConfig). Metrics engine: the MetricsServer.Source contribution (a source's metrics and breakdowns bound to their evaluators), the served metrics.catalog / metrics.query / metrics.details live values evaluating any of them through the one tz-aware bucketing engine — each query and drill-down (its key-range pages and its total) watching its source's `changes` through one refcounted subscription per source — and the sqlFlow / sqlLevel helpers joining a table against the engine's intervals.

          - `FakeSharedWorkers` — The browser's SharedWorker registry: one REAL `createSharedWsHost` per worker name (the production worker's logic, in-process), shared by every tab; `make(name)` is the `makeSharedWorker` factory, connecting a fresh `MessageChannel` to that host like the worker's `connect` event.
          - `FakeWebSocket` — A `WebSocketLike` with no network.
          - `FakeWsServer` — A no-network WebSocket server: `connect` is the bound `makeWebSocket` factory; every socket it ever handed out is retained for introspection (`all`), and the currently-OPEN subset (`openSockets`) is derived live from `readyState` so it is the single source of truth for the one-socket invariant.
          - `renderWithTransport` — `render(ui)` under a `<TransportProvider>` — what every component reading `useTransport()` (the endpoints hooks, `useLive`) needs, since the context has no default.
          - `testTransport` — A page-shaped transport for a test: same-origin sockets (`SharedWebSocket`), the global `fetch` read at call time (so a fetch the test stubs answers), assets loaded by their own path, the computer behind it, and its telemetry reported — each overridable.
          - `transportWrapper` — A `wrapper` (`render` / `renderHook`) mounting `transport` above the tree.
          - Types: `FakeWsServerOptions`, `RenderWithTransportOptions`, `TabHandle`, `TransportHub`

    - **`undo-redo`** — Surface-scoped client-side undo/redo command-history stack: a UndoRedoProvider per surface tab holding past/future stacks of {undo,redo} thunks, with time-windowed coalescing, a max-depth cap, a re-entrancy guard so replayed patches aren't re-recorded, mount-scoped entries (useScopedUndoRedo drops its entries when its mount unmounts), a pending-flush seam (usePendingFlush / registerPendingFlush: a producer holding a not-yet-recorded entry seals it at the start of every undo/redo turn, outside the replay guard, so it is the entry popped), serialized turns (an undo/redo during an in-flight thunk queues FIFO behind it instead of running under the guard), and an optional useUndoRedoShortcuts (mod+z / mod+shift+z / mod+y) convenience binding.

Adaptive-bar report kind: validates the adaptive-bar primitive's layout-contract fault payloads (no-slack = the bar was given no room to give, nested-bar = a measuring bar was written inside another bar's occupant so both claim the same row's slack, row-overflow = on a converged pass the fit blessed the row as fitting and the occupants still stick out of the bar's own content box, no-convergence = the placement never settled, iframe-relocation = a frame the browser cannot move without reloading, empty-rung = a widget declared a smaller form and rendered nothing as it), fingerprints by fault + origin (the innermost UI-context node above the bar's root, falling back to the label that several unrelated bars share) + overflow mode + the offending occupant's id, excluding the per-occurrence lineage path, round evidence and message so one broken bar = one row, and renders a per-fault task — what the bar did instead, the consumer-side fix, and for no-convergence the recorded rounds naming which occupant resized itself. Re-arms periodically (6h) since a broken host re-produces the fault on every mount.
      - Web:

- **`runs`** — The merged run surface: <RunsDataView> over the `runs` union window (a live scroll: base fields derived from the collection and presented once, plus every arm's own fields, derived from its liveArm, each bound to its column), and the seams an arm reaches it through: runLinks (where its rows go — data-view's CollectionRowActivation over the arm), investigateRuns, and Runs.Leading for the list row's status glyph; the kind filter's options are the registered arms, derived by every list; an arm presents its fields' cells with FieldPresentation.Register({ owner: arm }). Every row is a single field-driven line; a domain's detail lives in the pane its rows open. Also exports useRun (a live point read of one run by its (kind, id) pair) and <RunDuration> (finished duration, or a running run's ticking elapsed time). The merged run space as ONE routed union window (a Meta-DataView): runsServed serves the `runs` collection's window, its `:rows` point read (useRun) and `:groups` from every arm bound through runsServed.arm — a domain's own ledger typed against the base row and its liveArm, the ledger id and the duration derived by the union — so a write to one ledger refills only the rows it changed. Names no run kind.
  - Web:
    - Slots: `Runs.Leading`

    - **`automations`** — Automations in the agent manager: the Automations sidebar entry and list (a DataView over the catalog — trigger in words, next run, on/off, open task), the detail pane (Run now through Background activity; Behavior — enabled, model, push policy; Trigger — schedule presets or custom cron, or the event and its settle wait; the sections an automation contributes through Automations.Section; its sources; the Prompt template with Customized / Reset to default — PromptTemplateBlock, the same editor for any template field an automation declares; and the History of the tasks it filed or started — each row expandable into the Automations.TaskDetail contributions for its task), the presentation of the exposed `origin` Automation field in every list whose rows reach a task (its options the live catalog), and automationConfigContributions — how a declaring plugin registers its automation's config document (Automations.Config). Automations registry: defineAutomation declares something that files a task and launches its agent on its own (file kind) or launches agents on existing tasks a few at a time (launch kind: candidates, launched ONLY when a person approved them — the tasks_ext_launch_decision side-table, written by the decide-launch endpoint alone — concurrency slots held until a task settles or releaseLaunchedTask, and a maxLaunches batch per turn-on after which it turns itself off), and owns its job (automation.<id>) — its config document (defineAutomationConfig: enabled, push policy, model, excluded sources, trigger — a schedule re-installed live on change, or an event whose bursts settle into one run — and the prompt template), the one-open-task dedupe, the filled prompt, the filing (task + category + tasks_ext_origin row in one transaction) and the armed launch. Serves the automations.launch-decisions.all set, exposes the filing automation to every list whose rows reach a task (the `origin` field), and notifies the bell when an automated task needs its person. The automations.catalog value and the automations.tasks collection (the origin side-table, an automation's history) are the machine half's.

    - **`outcome-report`** — The outcome report an automated task's agent submitted: a card at the end of the transcript of the conversation that wrote it (scrolling with it, not pinned over it) (markdown body, pushed / branch-waiting / no-changes standing, and its question as one-click answers sent as the next turn), and OutcomeReportDetail — the same report read-only, shown in an expanded row of an automation's History (Automations.TaskDetail).     - **`sidequest-autopilot`** — The Sidequest autopilot in the Automations pane: registers its config (enabled, at once, in total, push policy, model, prompt, triage, stale after, triage prompt) and contributes its sections — Launch list (a DataView of every ready sidequest in launch order, grouped Approved / Proposed by triage / Needs your call / Looks obsolete / Triaging / Excluded; each row expands to triage's context, its one-click question and Re-triage; triage may tick a row, only Approve selected approves), Run until (until you turn it off, or until a date and time after which it turns itself off) and Triage (the switch, stale after, the triage prompt). Declares the Sidequest autopilot automation (launch kind, off by default): while on, it starts agents on the ready sidequests (no attempt, not held, dropped or blocked) a person APPROVED in its launch list — best first by triage's value for size, `concurrency` at a time (default 2), at most `maxLaunches` per turn-on (default 5) — each with the autopilot prompt (triage's context and the person's answer included; never ask, check obsolescence first, stay in scope, push only what the push policy allows, finish with submit_outcome_report). Triage (on by default, main only): each ready sidequest is read once by a read-only Sonnet run (Read / Grep / Glob over the main checkout) — verdict ready / decide / split / obsolete, risk, size, value, areas, a free-form context and at most one one-click question — stored in tasks_ext_sidequest_triage and served as the sidequest-autopilot.triage.all set; queued when a task becomes a sidequest or a sidequest becomes ready, backfilled at boot, re-run only by the person's Re-triage. Triage approves nothing. Turns itself off at its `runUntil`.

    - **`icons`** — Draws icons: <Icon icon={symbol(…)} active?/> renders an IconRef from the page's inline SVG sprites in its theme scope's icon style. A leaf below the ui-kit — it knows no theme: the icons token group publishes each scope's style (usePublishIconStyle), <Theme> boundaries say which scope an icon is in (IconScopeProvider), and the sprites plugin fills and mounts the sheet. Icon families beyond Material are contributed to Icons.Family (Lucide is this plugin's own; an app draws its own with defineIconFamily), published to <Icon> by IconFamilyHost. Reads glyphs out of the installed Iconify JSON: resolveIcon (a name in a set, aliases followed), resolveSymbol (the icon drawing a symbol in a style, after the nearest-style fallback) and symbolBody (one Material Symbols glyph in a style, for a consumer with no sprite sheet — the release CLI's app icon); SETI_SET / readSetiSet expose the vendored Seti file-type set (jesseweed/seti-ui, MIT, one colour).

        - **`saved-themes`** — Saved themes (tweakcn imports and custom themes) as a resident theme source read live (saved-themes.list, hydrated before first paint), plus useEditTheme — the one place theme edits land, copying a read-only theme into a custom one on first edit — useAwaitSavedThemesWrite, which resolves once the list has re-read a write, and useRemoveSavedTheme. - **`upstream`** — Registers the Upstream merges automation's config (schedule, push policy, model, prompt template) for the Automations pane and Settings → Config. Daily upstream.detect-updates job (main only): when the repo this checkout was cloned from has commits local `main` does not, it records one rolling `upstream-updates-available` report — the bell and Debug → Reports, whose Investigate mints a merge task. And the Upstream merges automation (upstream-merge; off by default, daily once on, editable from the Automations pane): when upstream is ahead and no merge task is open, it files ONE auto-started task (Upstream category, linked to the report) whose agent runs `./singularity upstream merge`, builds and checks the app, and lands it only as far as its Push setting allows (never, by default).
